fields.meta_description: Build a Stripe donation form with monthly tiers and a fund picker, and keep a record of every paid gift in a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Stripe Donation Form With Gifts in Your Own Database
fields.hero_description: Build a Stripe donation form that takes one-time and monthly gifts and saves each paid gift to a donor table you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens Before and After a Donor Pays
fields.features_subheading: A Stripe donation form asks your questions, hands payment to Stripe, and writes each paid gift to your records.
fields.feature_1:
Your questions first, then Stripe's checkout

The form asks for the fund and a dedication, plus once or monthly, then sends the donor to Stripe Checkout. Set the submit type to donate and the pay button reads Donate.
fields.feature_2:
Gifts recorded from Stripe's payment event

Stripe creates a checkout.session.completed event when someone pays. The app writes the gift and its fund to your table from that event, next to the Stripe payment ID.
fields.feature_3:
One donor row, every gift beneath it

Each donor gets one row in a database you own, with every gift and its fund listed under it. Search a name before a phone call and see a full giving history on one screen.
fields.feature_4:
A thank-you email that names the fund

The app emails each donor once the gift is recorded, with the amount and the fund they picked. Monthly donors get one each time their gift renews, with the renewal date.
fields.feature_5:
New funds added by asking for them

Describe a change in plain English, such as a spring roof fund or a fourth monthly tier, and Emergent rebuilds the form and the table behind it. Nothing is redrawn by hand.
fields.feature_6:
Code that moves with your nonprofit

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository when the donation form has to sit inside a site your developer runs. Host it anywhere and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Nonprofits Use Stripe for Gifts
fields.tab_content_1:
Not a one-time gift but $15 a month from Linnea

Bellwick Community Radio asks members to give monthly at $8, $15, or $30. The tiers are fixed because Stripe's pay-what-you-want prices do not support recurring payments. Linnea Nyberg picks $15, and the form starts a Stripe subscription in her name. Her donor row shows the tier and her next gift on Dec 9.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each gift counts toward one of 3 library funds

Gwynne Public Library Foundation lists 3 funds on its form: the book fund, the teen room, and greatest need. The fund a donor picks is saved with the gift. This month the dashboard shows $2,340 for books, $1,180 for the teen room, and $860 for greatest need, or $4,380 in all.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 46 gifts come in from guests' own phones

Forty-six guests at the Quenby Street Theater benefit give at intermission, each from a phone at their seat. The amount starts at $40, and each guest raises or lowers it before paying. By the final curtain the lobby screen shows $3,915 raised, with every gift in the table under the guest's name.
fields.tab_content_4:
Only Imogen hears of gifts of $1,000 or more

Imogen Quarles runs Oxbow Ridge Land Trust, and any gift of $1,000 or more reaches her as a Slack direct message. Rafferty Gale gives $2,500 to the trail easement fund. The message carries his name and phone number beside the amount. She calls him that afternoon to thank him.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Stripe Donation Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a Stripe donation form that sends donors to Stripe Checkout and records every paid gift in a table you own.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the ways people give you money
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide what to ask before checkout
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every way gifts arrive today, such as one-time gifts after a newsletter, monthly support, and giving at an annual event. Each one becomes a choice on the form or a separate form. Keep pledges and auction bids out, since those are not paid at once.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the fund choice, any tribute name, and contact details on your own form. Stripe Checkout's custom fields hold up to 3 extra questions. Anything beyond that has to come before the donor reaches Stripe. Leave card details to Stripe's page.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Offer 3 or 4 preset amounts and an open field for one-time gifts. Monthly gifts run as Stripe subscriptions, which use fixed prices. Give monthly donors set tiers to pick from. Put the amount above the contact fields.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the funds and the amounts into one prompt, along with what should happen after each gift. Emergent builds the form, the donor table behind it, and a screen for whoever reviews gifts. Change any of it later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the Stripe account you already take payments with. The app opens checkout through it and reads each payment back into the donor table. Store the secret key in the app's settings and never paste it into the form page itself.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Pick who hears about each gift
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose what each donor gets after paying, such as an email that names the fund. Then set a threshold for gifts a person should see the same day, and name that person. A board chair or a development lead both work.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run the whole flow in a Stripe sandbox, which simulates transactions with test values. Give once and start a monthly gift. Check that both rows land in the donor table and that the thank-you email arrives before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a Stripe donation form?
faq_plan.a: A Stripe donation form is an online giving form that takes each gift through a Stripe account. The donor picks an amount and answers a few questions, such as the fund, then pays on Stripe's checkout page. The organization gets a record of the gift for the receipt and the thank-you.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a Stripe donation form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in Emergent's AI form builder: the funds and preset amounts, plus who hears about each gift. Emergent builds the form and the donor table it writes to. Connect your payment account, run a test gift, and share the link once both rows look right.

faq_plan.q: Can donors choose their own amount on a Stripe donation form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for one-time gifts. Stripe's customer-chooses-price option is made for tips and donations, and it lets a donor type any amount on the payment page. Pair it with a few preset buttons on your own form, since a suggested figure gives undecided donors a place to start.

faq_plan.q: Should a Stripe donation form ask for the fund before or after payment?
faq_plan.a: Before. Ask for the fund on your own form and send it to checkout with the gift, and the payment and the fund arrive in the same record. The order holds for any donation form: amount and fund first, contact details after. On Emergent, that record sits in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Why should a Stripe donation form record gifts from the payment event?
faq_plan.a: So that no paid gift goes unrecorded. Stripe's guide notes that a customer can pay successfully and then lose their internet connection before your landing page loads. The app records the gift from the payment event instead, whether or not that page ever loads.

faq_plan.q: Can I put a Stripe donation form on my existing website?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the form behind the Donate button on your site, or place it on the donate page in an embed block. Test the embedded version on a phone, where the payment step is easiest to break. Every gift from the embedded form still lands in the database you own on Emergent.

faq_plan.q: Can a Stripe donation form take auction bids at a gala?
faq_plan.a: Not well. A gift is paid the moment it is made, while a bid is a promise that turns into a payment only if it wins. Take bids on a silent auction form and charge the winners at the end of the night. Keep the Stripe donation form for gifts made in the room.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a Stripe donation form ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what the gift and its record need: the amount, the fund, a name, and an email. Add a tribute or employer-match question only if someone on staff will act on the answer. Then fill the form on a phone and cut any field you would not miss.

faq_plan.q: How many gifts can a Stripe donation form take in one day?
faq_plan.a: As many as donors send. Emergent is free to start, the free tier covers building and publishing, and a form built on it has no response caps. A giving day that brings in 900 gifts by noon keeps taking them into the afternoon.

faq_plan.q: Should an animal rescue use the same Stripe donation form for adoptions?
faq_plan.a: No, use two forms. An adoption follows an application and an approval, and that flow belongs on a pet adoption form with its own review step. The Stripe donation form stays open to anyone, with funds such as medical care or food, and no application in front of the gift.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook and every AlsoAsked question is about Stripe the company, so the page answers the builder: a Stripe donation form is the nonprofit's own form (amount, fund, monthly choice, dedication) that hands the payment to Stripe Checkout and records each paid gift from Stripe's completed-payment event in a donor table the nonprofit owns. It wins on the Stripe-specific details guides skip: custom amounts cannot recur, so monthly gifts need fixed tiers; the Donate button label; why gifts are recorded from the event and not the thank-you page; testing in a sandbox.
